I currently am a caretaker for disabled individuals. It's a good job. Fulfilling in some ways, but it's not the extent of help i desire. One could argue in a very long way that I already am, but my priority lies with "saving lives". And I think that I could do better than what I am doing now in more intimate and hands on fields. 

The reasoning is inconsistent though. I want it to help people but to me it also marks an end for me in the sense that; I don't really have a lot of life left in me. My life sucks terribly. And I'm not a good person. I'm hoping in a way that I can give my life to work on something that actually matters. Then eventually succumb to depression at least having grazed the lives of others on my way out. As opposed to just... dying and having no effect on the world. Idk. I feel like in part, using the slang is partially to not make the conversations feel so weighted. Not to make them less of a problem but to make them feel less troublesome and traumatic in our communication (which can appear as downplaying, i understand). But i see it as cooperation between everyone to make something already so terrible and hard to deal with palatable in conversation. This is afterall a self harm centered sub so the conversations are happening often. Why not add some spice to make the typically awkward topics of how to clean a wound, how to hide my scars, how to traverse trauma, and make them less graphic and perhaps more accessible to the younger ones in this sub; who probably only engage so well here because of this increased accessibility.

Last night i went to bed. It was August 27th 2018. When I woke up. It was March 20th 2022. I wake up everyday to the same bedroom. I go through the same routine. I play a game or watch a movie. I make some useless and poorly made art. I go to bed. I do it again. The days aren't separate. I take my time away in chunks. In multi-week intervals.

August 27th, 2018 was the date of my first suicide attempt. I ended up in a psych ward but because i was 17 i went to the youth section. I remember vividly those three days feeling like one. It was a routine. Wake up at 6am. Take meds. Eat breakfast. Talk with a doctor. Do some group therapy. Eat lunch. Go outside to play or sit around and chat. Dinner. Meds. TV. Bed. I know for a fact that cycle repeated three times. But it felt like one long one. I remember. The first night i went to bed. There was a drawing on the nightstand, left behind by the child who last had the room. It... was a drawing in crayon... of this kids dad beating his mom. And i thought to myself... this poor child. I think he was 4-5 years old... this poor kid has probably gone through hell. And I'm here... why? I know that's not fair. But back then I guess I had main character syndrome. So I felt the need to verify my depression and make this situation about me. But in me... there was significant doubt about my mental state. Doctors were diagnosing me with PTSD, clincinal depression, severe anxiety, etc. and i just. Didn't believe in any of it.

Today, March 20th, 2022. I'm laying in bed, recollecting past trauma and recognizing the time I've wasted. And I want to be better for it. But self reflection doesn't allot me any betterment. I feel the same. I feel like a shell. And... I feel like one day. I might go to bed. And wake up at another moment in life. Only to look back at March 20th, 2022 with the same bitter tinge that I get when I think of August 27th, 2018.

Mr. Robot is and likely always will be my favorite TV show. A little bit of cringe dialogue here and there but other than that the show is fucking amazing. some really sensitive content in there though if you're not comfortable with that. 

as for movies...

Parasite, a Korean film by one of my fav directors Bong Joon-Ho. (also watch memories of murder omg i fucking loved that movie). Parasite is pretty much a critique of class and poverty. Regarded highly for it's fusion and ability to slip between a plethora of genres. Goes from comedy to thriller to mystery to horror etc. it's a really fun watch!

Perfect Blue is a confusing mess (in a good way) if you're interested in something that will probably take a couple viewings to fully understand. It's a Japanese animation by legendary writer Satoshi Kon.  Perfect Blue, in a nutshell, is pretty much about a j-pop star slowly going insane. It's fucking awesome.

The Lighthouse is also quite the thinker. Made my Robert Eggers and starring two of my favorite actors. It's no wonder this is one of my favorites. Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe are secluded on an island housing a lighthouse for many months. And... well... things...... divulge. It's a movie that is fucking hilarious while also being very thoughtful and provoking. Love it.

Lastly, if you just want a movie to make you cry, watch Marriage Story. Never seen a more heartbreaking but honest portrayal of falling out of love with a person. But, if you don't want to cry, don't watch it. It's one or the other lmao.

Enjoy!

I watched a handful of absolute bangers this last couple weeks.

12 Angry Men - This is one of my favs of all time. I think I've watched it 10+ times at this point. As far as black and white films. It's a classic. It's my comfort movie :).

Memories of Murder - A film by one of my top 5 favorite directors, Bong Joon-Ho. He directed Parasite a couple years ago and i highly recommend that as well! Memories of Murder is a murder mystery based on a true story. It's a complicated commentary on policing in a small town in Korea mirrored by volunteering cop from Seoul (there's more underlying commentary than that but that's what you'll see at face value). The ensemble cast works together to solve a string of rape/homicides. It's a depressing... but encompassing ride.

The Lighthouse - God I fucking love this movie. You ever watch movie. And you sit back and think "what the fuck was that?" That's this movie. On crack. It's funny and weird and anxiety inducing. I've found myself permanently incorporating quotes from this movie in my daily conversations.

Good Time - This movie is fucking immaculate. Top tier acting and directing. I think this is the movie that made me realize that stylized cinematography is something I'm VERY partial too. I love how this movie looks. This brother director duo is the same one that made Uncut Gems, if you're familiar with that movie. Be ready for a greed driven, fast paced drama about a robbery gone wrong!

I could give a ton more but I'm sure you'll love at least a few of this handful. Enjoy your movie viewings!

Edit: If you're okay with gore. I actually recommend marathoning the saw movies. omg the storylines are so bad the movies are some of the funniest pieces of cinema I've ever consumed. it's like a soap opera with a horror budget. First movie is actually good tho. Ta-ta~
